## About

The YAML header sets the viewer's colors without CSS, giving a deep blue
backdrop, a cream caption band, dark brown caption text, and rust links. Every
image on the page gets them.

```yaml
panzoom:
  backdrop: "rgba(18, 52, 86, 0.92)"  # deep blue
  caption-background: "#f4e9d8"       # cream
  caption-color: "#3b2a1a"            # dark brown
  link-color: "#a0361b"               # rust
```

Each option sets one of the viewer's CSS variables; [styling with
CSS](n-css-class.html) sets the same variables from a stylesheet, for some pages
only. A single image or code cell can set its own colors, as cases 2 and 4 show;
they apply while that image is open.

## 1. Markdown image {#c1 expect-open="panzoom" expect-overlay="rgba(18, 52, 86, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(244, 233, 216)"}

```markdown {.show-source}
![An image with `.panzoom`. It opens with the colors set on this page, a deep blue backdrop and a cream caption band, and this [link](https://quarto.org) is rust.](../../images/mv-0.jpg){.panzoom fig-alt="Sunset over a sandy beach, with a tall rock stack against the sun"}
```

## 2. Colors for one image {#c2 expect-open="panzoom" expect-overlay="rgba(20, 60, 40, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(232, 243, 234)"}

```markdown {.show-source}
![An image with `.panzoom`, with colors of its own, set as attributes. It opens with a deep green backdrop and a pale green caption band instead of the colors set on this page, and this [link](https://quarto.org) is dark green.](../../images/mv-1.jpg){.panzoom backdrop="rgba(20, 60, 40, 0.92)" caption-background="#e8f3ea" caption-color="#173d24" link-color="#0b6b3a" fig-alt="Waves breaking below grassy clay cliffs at Aquinnah"}
```

## 3. Code cell {#c3 expect-open="panzoom" expect-overlay="rgba(18, 52, 86, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(244, 233, 216)"}

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of vapor pressure rising steeply with temperature"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   A code cell with `panzoom: true`. It opens with the blue and cream colors
#|   set on this page, as case 1 does.

plot(pressure, type = "b", pch = 19)
```

## 4. Colors for one cell {#c4 expect-open="panzoom" expect-overlay="rgba(70, 25, 15, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(251, 233, 220)"}

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| panzoom:
#|   backdrop: "rgba(70, 25, 15, 0.92)"
#|   caption-background: "#fbe9dc"
#|   caption-color: "#4a1f10"
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   A code cell with colors of its own, under `#| panzoom:`. It opens with a
#|   dark red backdrop and a peach caption band.

plot(cars, pch = 19)
```

## 5. Gallery with mixed colors {#c5 expect-open="panzoom" expect-steps="true"}

A gallery of three images, two with colors of their own. Each image shows its
own colors while it is open, and the next or previous image doesn't keep them.

```markdown {.show-source}
![The first of three images in a gallery, with colors of its own. It opens with a deep green backdrop and a pale green caption band.](../../images/mv-2.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" backdrop="rgba(20, 60, 40, 0.92)" caption-background="#e8f3ea" caption-color="#173d24" fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky" expect-overlay="rgba(20, 60, 40, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(232, 243, 234)"}

![The second image, with no colors of its own. It shows the blue and cream colors set on this page, not the first image's green.](../../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path" expect-overlay="rgba(18, 52, 86, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(244, 233, 216)"}

![The third image, with colors of its own again. It shows a dark red backdrop and a peach caption band.](../../images/mv-4.jpg){.panzoom group="mixed" backdrop="rgba(70, 25, 15, 0.92)" caption-background="#fbe9dc" caption-color="#4a1f10" fig-alt="A sailboat with a flag-striped sail off a sandy beach" expect-overlay="rgba(70, 25, 15, 0.92)" expect-band="rgb(251, 233, 220)"}
```
